title: Hierarchical target-fusion autoscaling engine for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a Hierarchical Target-Fusion Autoscaling Engine (HTFAE) for Redwood Dedicated fleets that merges multiple target signals (latency p95, token throughput, queued requests per tenant, and committed throughput contracts) into a single scaling decision. The engine must support: (1) per-tenant and fleet-level targets, (2) multi-timescale scoring (instantaneous, short-window, long-window), (3) pluggable scaling algorithms (proportional-step, derivative damping, conservative PID variant), and (4) safety fences (rate limits, maximum surge percentage, cooldown windows, contract-aware throttles). Focus is on predictable throughput guarantees for committed fleets while limiting cost exposure and avoiding oscillation during bursty traffic.
background: Current autoscalers either optimize a single metric (p95 latency or token throughput) or run a composition of heuristics that are hard to reason about when tenants have mixed SLAs (best-effort vs committed). We've seen two classes of failures in Dedicated: 1) overprovisioning during short spikes leading to cost spikes, 2) oscillations when a tenant with a large burst causes scale up followed immediately by scale down. HTFAE should provide deterministic, auditable scaling decisions and explicit tie-ins to contracted throughput guarantees.
goals: Merge heterogeneous signals into one actionable scale intent at fleet and per-tenant granularity
Provide deterministic safety limits: max surge %, max scale rate (nodes/min), cooldown enforcement
Enable operator-visible scoring breakdowns in Console for troubleshooting
Ship a simulator that validates policies against historical tenant traces
Integrate contract-aware headroom so dedicated fleets honor committed throughput before best-effort consumption
non_goals: Implement model-level kernel tuning (out of scope for this ticket)
design_decisions: Use weighted fusion of normalized metrics rather than hard cascades to avoid priority inversion
Expose 3 timescales: instant (10s), short (2m), long (15m) and aggregate with tunable weights
Default scaling algorithm will be Proportional-Step with derivative damping; later pluggable PID-like variant for experiments
Safety limits enforced as policy layer after a scale intent is produced: surge cap, per-tenant max nodes, global node rate limit
Keep early-stage rollout to non-production dedicated pools and one enterprise customer under feature flag
tradeoffs: Weighted fusion simplifies decision visibility but may hide edge cases where a single metric should veto scaling (we will add explicit veto rules later)
Proportional-Step is simpler and more predictable than full PID, but may require manual tuning per fleet; we mitigate with simulator and default heuristics
Enforcing contract-first headroom can underutilize capacity for best-effort tenants during sustained low load, which is acceptable for committed SLA correctness
implementation_notes: Controller will run in control-plane with compiled policy; scale intents are gossiped to fleet-orchestrator which executes node lifecycle
Metrics normalization: convert p95 ms to a unitless score [0..1] using baseline SLO and saturated cap, throughput compared to committed units, queue depth sigmoid mapping
Simulator will be kept in repository sim/autoscale-sim and accept traces in ndjson format; include a dry-run mode that produces intent timelines
Add audit events for each intent: reason vector, contributor weights, safety clamps applied, resulting node delta
Telemetry: add per-decision histogram of scale magnitude, decision latency, and safety-clamp triggers for Console charts
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests for metric fusion logic with synthetic signals
Simulator reproduces known oscillation incident (INC-2025-114) and shows mitigated outcome under HTFAE policy
End-to-end test: flagged fleet in staging honors committed throughput >= 99% over 1h synthetic burst while respecting surge cap
Console shows per-decision breakdown and safety clamp annotations for 7 days of retention in staging
Feature flag gating and rollout doc prepared with rollback plan
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: improper normalization leads to over-weighting a noisy metric. Mitigation: add guardband and clipping, require signal stability before full weight applies
Risk: latency of decision cycle causes delayed response. Mitigation: keep instant timescale lightweight and benchmark decision path end-to-end
Risk: safety fences too strict cause inability to meet SLAs. Mitigation: simulation and canary on low-risk fleets, add operator override path
